title: Northwestern Medicine & Techstars Healthcare Accelerator
deadline_note: Closed. The current cycle (third class, program March 8 – June 3, 2027) opened August 24, 2026 and its final deadline was November 18, 2026 at 11:59pm PST. The next cycle has not been announced. The program has run one class a year starting in March, so the next opening may not come until around August 2027; that is an inference, not a published date.
amount: $220,000 investment: $200,000 uncapped MFN Safe + $20,000 convertible equity agreement for 5% common stock (equity, not a grant)

summary.at_a_glance: Health tech accelerator run by Techstars with Northwestern Medicine, held in person at Northwestern Medicine's Mansueto Innovation Institute in Chicago for a class of six startups. It is still running: the third class starts March 8, 2027, but applications for it closed on November 18, 2026. No later application dates are published yet.
summary.what_they_offer: $220,000 investment per company, three months of in-person support at the Mansueto Innovation Institute in Chicago ending in a Demo Day (June 3, 2027 for the current class), mentorship and collaboration with Northwestern Medicine clinical and technical experts, access to the Techstars network of investors, partners and alumni, and partner perks valued at more than $4M.
summary.what_theyre_looking_for: Program focus: 'investing in key areas like access to care, artificial intelligence, and digital therapeutics', and companies 'enhancing patient experience, improving physician and nursing efficiency, and advancing the frontier in precision medicine, robotics, and cybersecurity'. Techstars' general ranking of criteria: team, team, team, then market, traction (progress), idea.
summary.who_can_apply: Early-stage startups from most countries; no co-founder, revenue or finished product is required, and solo founders are accepted. Teams must be able to be legally present in the program's country during the program, and companies 'should be organized to receive U.S. venture funding'. Techstars invests in US corporations or foreign equivalents; companies that are not yet incorporated can apply. Companies based in or doing business in Russia, North Korea, Iran, Syria, Cuba, Venezuela or the Crimea, Donetsk or Luhansk regions cannot apply. Founders apply to one program per application cycle and can name a second choice.
summary.how_to_apply: 1) Create a Techstars account at apply.techstars.com. 2) Step 1 Founder Profile: About You, then Demographics. 3) Step 2 Accelerator Application: Startup Details, Startup Team, Startup Progress, Startup Strategy, Connections & Referrals; saving the last section submits the application to the general Techstars pool. 4) Step 3 Program Selection: pick this program as primary preference (and optionally an alternate) before applications close at 11:59pm PST on the deadline date. 5) If a program team is interested, the applicant is asked for more: Supplemental Questions and a Techstars Deal Terms question appear in the same portal. 6) First and second-round interviews, with invitations typically one to four weeks after the deadline, then a screening committee for finalists. Every applicant is told their status; Techstars says to expect an answer within 60–90 days of applying or about 4 weeks after applications close.
summary.worth_noting: The application portal stays open year-round: an application completed after the deadline is 'added to a general pool for consideration', with no promise on when Techstars will respond. This is an equity investment, not a grant: Techstars takes 5% common stock via the $20K agreement plus whatever the $200K uncapped MFN Safe converts into. Techstars invests in US corporations or foreign equivalents, which matters for an LLC applicant. The program is in person in Chicago and takes only six companies per class. The official name is 'Northwestern Medicine & Techstars Healthcare Accelerator' (the old record called it 'Northwestern Medicine Techstars'). The application form is the same as for every other Techstars accelerator; the only Chicago-related item in the first round is the optional 'Chicago, United States' affiliation choice in 'Connections & Referrals'. The form has tight character limits (400–500 characters for most answers).

portal.platform: Custom Techstars application system (apply.techstars.com, Keycloak login at login.techstars.com)
portal.notes: Opening apply.techstars.com redirects straight to a 'Create a Techstars account' page (First name, Last name, Email, Sign up) with a Log in link; nothing of the form is visible before that. No CAPTCHA is present on the sign-up page; pages after login were not seen. Three steps: Step 1 Founder Profile (About You, then Demographics), Step 2 Accelerator Application (Startup Details, Startup Team, Startup Progress, Startup Strategy, Connections & Referrals), Step 3 Program Selection (primary and alternate program). Each section saves only when all required fields are filled and 'Save & Continue' is pressed; the last section's button is 'Save Application', which submits the application to the general pool. Answers can be edited later and the same application is reused across terms (one accelerator application per account). Co-founders are invited by name and email from the dashboard and each completes their own Founder Profile. One file upload: pitch deck, PDF only, max 10 MB. Video fields accept YouTube links only. Long answers show a live character counter. The site states that completing the application takes 30–60 minutes.

questions_note: The real form is at apply.techstars.com and sits behind a Techstars account login, so the rendered form was NOT seen. The questions here come from two official Techstars sources. (1) The official Application Preview page (techstars.com/application-preview), which lists the question topics for all accelerators. (2) The form definitions that ship in the public JavaScript of the application app itself (apply.techstars.com/main.a12a33d804e57f102763.js, downloaded 2026-11-24 without logging in), which give the exact labels, help text, options, required flags and character limits used above. The two sources agree topic by topic; where the wording differs, the app's wording is used (for example the preview says "What problem is your company looking to solve?" and the app says "What problem are you looking to solve?"). Confidence is high but not complete: the Founder Profile 'About You' page is rendered straight from these definitions, while the other sections are fetched from Techstars' API after login and could differ slightly from the copy in the JavaScript. Could not be seen: the options of "Which vertical networks are relevant to your company?", the full city and country lists, and the list of programs in Step 3. Text inside [square brackets] in a help field is my annotation (display conditions, validation rules), not wording from the form. A public feature flag read on page load (pitch-deck-upload = on) shows the pitch deck is currently a required PDF upload; the older "Pitch deck URL" field is hidden while that flag is on. The form is the same for every Techstars accelerator: there is no separate question set per program in the first-round application. Program-specific content is limited to the affiliation options in 'Connections & Referrals' (CareFirst, Baltimore, Chicago, Johns Hopkins, USC) and the program choice in Step 3. NOT included above: the second-round 'Supplemental Questions I / II' and 'Techstars Deal Terms' sections, which appear only if a program team invites the applicant ("Good news! Our program teams want to learn more about your company."). The app holds a bank of about 50 such questions (team, customers, finances, cap table, pitch video, plus program-specific ones such as Johns Hopkins, CareFirst and Baltimore-area relationship questions); which ones an applicant gets is decided on Techstars' side. They are saved verbatim in the evidence file form-definition-extract.txt. Also not included: the co-founder invite dialog (name and email per co-founder), whose exact field labels were not visible.
